ACTION: ADD
TITLE: pairing pre-training for vision and language
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel pre-training strategy, Pairing Pre-training for Vision and Language (PPVL), to improve the representation power of HOI detectors by leveraging the relationship between vision and language. PPVL pre-trains the visual and language encoders jointly on a large-scale image-text dataset, where the image-text pairs are curated to have a specific interaction context. This pre-training stage allows the visual and language encoders to learn a common semantic space, enhancing their ability to capture rich interaction features. We will fine-tune the pre-trained detector on various HOI benchmarks and evaluate its performance using standard metrics, such as mAP and precision at each interact type. Controls will include a standard object detector trained from scratch, a baseline HOI detector without PPVL pre-training, and an ablation study of PPVL pre-training.

CONTROLS: baseline object detector, baseline HOI detector, ablation study of PPVL pre-training. Evaluate all methods on the same held-out test set and report the mean and standard deviation over five seeds.
COST: 60 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: mAP 2-4% improvement over baseline HOI detectors; could fail if the pre-trained knowledge does not generalize well to HOI tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: attentional localization maps for hoi
PROPOSAL: Develop an Attentional Localization Maps (ALM) for HOI detection to improve the spatial localization of interactions. ALM generates attention maps for each interaction class, focusing on the specific regions of the objects and humans that are relevant for the interaction. This is achieved through an attention mechanism that attends to the feature maps of the objects and humans based on the class labels. We will integrate ALM with our composable HOI detection framework and evaluate its performance on various HOI benchmarks. Controls will include a standard object detector without ALM, a baseline HOI detector with ALM, and an ablation study of ALM.

CONTROLS: baseline object detector, baseline HOI detector with ALM, ablation study of ALM. Include a matched-compute baseline that receives the same training budget and hyperparameter search as the proposed method.
COST: 80 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: improvement in mAP and precision at each interact type due to better spatial localization; could fail if ALM overfits to specific interactions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: multiple instance learning for interaction detection
PROPOSAL: Design a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) framework for HOI detection to effectively handle the multiple-interaction cases where a single image contains multiple unpicked-interaction between different humans and objects. MIL will treat each image as a bag of instances (human-object pairs) and the detector will learn to recognize the interactions within each bag. This will be achieved through a Max-Margin Learning formulation and an attention mechanism to selectively weigh the importance of each instance. We will evaluate the MIL framework on various HOI benchmarks and compare its performance with standard HOI detectors.

CONTROLS: baseline object detector, baseline HOI detector, ablation study of MIL and attention mechanism. Compare against the strongest published baseline for this problem, re-run with the same data, tuning budget and evaluation protocol.
COST: 90 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: improvement in mAP and precision at each interact type due to better handling of multiple-interaction cases; could fail if the MIL framework overfits to specific interactions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: generalized object connectivity graph for hoi
PROPOSAL: Propose a Generalized Object Connectivity Graph (GOCG) framework for HOI detection to model the complex relationships between humans and objects in a scene. GOCG will consist of edge attributes and multi-layer graph reasoning to capture various aspects of human-object interactions. We will use a multi-layer graph neural network to reason over the GOCG and improve HOI detection performance. We will evaluate GOCG on various HOI benchmarks and compare its performance with state-of-the-art HOI detectors.

CONTROLS: baseline object detector, baseline HOI detector, ablation study of GOCG and graph reasoning. Evaluate all methods on the same held-out test set and report the mean and standard deviation over five seeds.
COST: 110 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: improvement in mAP and precision at each interact type due to better modeling of human-object relationships; could fail if the GOCG framework overfits to specific interactions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: uncertainty-aware hoi detection
PROPOSAL: Develop an Uncertainty-Aware HOI Detection framework to quantify and utilize the uncertainty in HOI predictions. We will incorporate a probabilistic representation of the HOI predictions and use a Monte Carlo dropout technique to estimate the uncertainty of each prediction. This will allow us to perform uncertainty-aware inference and adapt to the ambiguity in human-object interactions. We will evaluate the Uncertainty-Aware HOI Detection framework on various HOI benchmarks and compare its performance with state-of-the-art HOI detectors.

CONTROLS: baseline object detector, baseline HOI detector, ablation study of uncertainty-aware inference. Include a matched-compute baseline that receives the same training budget and hyperparameter search as the proposed method.
COST: 100 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: improvement in mAP and precision at each interact type due to better handling of ambiguity in human-object interactions; could fail if the uncertainty-aware inference technique overfits to specific interactions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: temporal relationship modeling for hoi detection
PROPOSAL: Propose a Temporal Relationship Modeling (TRM) framework for HOI detection to capture the temporal dynamics of human-object interactions. TRM will utilize a graph neural network to model the temporal relationships between humans and objects and predict the next interaction state. We will integrate TRM with our existing composable HOI detection framework and evaluate its performance on video-based HOI benchmarks.

CONTROLS: baseline object detector, baseline HOI detector, ablation study of TRM and graph neural network. Compare against the strongest published baseline for this problem, re-run with the same data, tuning budget and evaluation protocol.
COST: 120 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: improvement in mAP and precision at each interact type due to better modeling of temporal relationships; could fail if the TRM framework overfits to specific interaction sequences. 

Note: this is the last experiment proposal before submission. A theoretical or inference-in-experiments conclusion could follow.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 7
TITLE: temporal relationship modeling for hoi detection
PROPOSAL: REVISED VERSION - In addition to the graph neural network, we will integrate a temporal convolutional network (TCN) to modeled the temporal evolution of human-object interactions. This will enable us to capture both local and global temporal dependencies in the interaction sequence. We will evaluate our revised TRM framework on video-based HOI benchmarks and compare its performance with state-of-the-art HOI detectors.

CONTROLS: baseline object detector, baseline HOI detector, ablation study of TRM and graph neural network, ablation study of TCN. Include a matched-compute baseline that receives the same training budget and hyperparameter search as the proposed method.
COST: 140 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected result: state-of-the-art performance in mAP and precision at each interact type due to better modeling of temporal relationships; could fail if the revised TRM framework overfits to specific interaction sequences.

Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique in machine learning, widely used for model compression, transfer learning, and improving generalization. Its core idea is to transfer knowledge from a "teacher" model to a (typically smaller) "student" model by training the student to match the teacher's output probabilities rather than categorical one-hot labels. This softened supervision has been shown to improve performance across a range of tasks. Consequently, a substantial body of research has focused on designing distillation mechanisms, such as dynamic temperature scaling, feature-based distillation, and task-aware teacher-student matching, typically assuming a large teacher that is optimized to maximize its own performance.

Despite its widespread adoption, the theoretical foundations of knowledge distillation remain only partially understood. In particular, the impact of the teacher's output probabilities on the student's optimization trajectory and generalization has not been fully characterized. Existing explanations attribute the usefulness of distillation to the regularizing effect of the teacher's soft estimates, to trade-offs such as precision versus recall or knowledge inheritance versus exploration, or to factors such as data geometry and optimization bias. Insights into how distillation affects the optimization itself have been developed only for special cases, such as self-distillation or a student that is a compressed version of the teacher, and rely on dedicated gradient approximations. A principled understanding of how distillation affects common learning algorithms, such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and its variants, for arbitrary teachers, is still lacking.

Recent works have begun to view distillation through a Bayesian lens, interpreting the teacher's outputs as (possibly noisy) estimates of the true class posterior probabilities of the data-generating distribution. From this statistical viewpoint, learning from accurate class posteriors has been argued to reduce the variance of the student's objective, and excess-risk and generalization bounds have been derived in terms of the distance between the teacher's predictions and the true posteriors. These analyses, however, characterize the statistical properties of the risk rather than the behavior of the learning algorithm that actually trains the student. The probabilistic perspective thus opens relatively unexplored questions about the dynamics of SGD-based learning under probabilistic supervision, and about how the statistical calibration of the teacher influences the student. Teacher calibration has been recognized as a key driver of distillation, but it remains unclear how the quality of the teacher's probability estimates should guide the way teachers are built.

This raises several questions. How does supervising a student with the exact class posterior probabilities, instead of one-hot labels, change the convergence behavior and stability of SGD-based learning and the generalization of the resulting student? In the realistic case where the teacher provides only imperfect, noisy estimates of these posteriors, how does the level of estimation error affect the student's convergence, generalization and accuracy, and under what conditions does probabilistic supervision remain preferable to one-hot labels? Finally, what practical guidelines follow for designing or choosing teacher models, beyond maximizing the teacher's own accuracy, so that their outputs provide better supervision for students trained with SGD-based optimizers?

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: exploring the teacher's calibration in knowledge distillation
PROPOSAL: Investigate how the statistical calibration of the teacher affects the student's convergence, generalization, and accuracy. Use a variant of the Wide ResNet-28-10 (WRN) as the teacher model, and a smaller version of the same architecture as the student. Train the teacher on a large image classification dataset (e.g., ImageNet) and evaluate the student on a held-out dataset (e.g., CIFAR-10). Vary the temperature of the soft labels generated by the teacher and measure the impact on the student's performance.
CONTROLS: Baseline: training the student with one-hot labels (no distillation); Ablations: removing temperature scaling from the soft labels.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the student's performance will improve with the teacher's calibration, and that an optimal temperature exists which maximizes this improvement, but that excessive temperature scaling will degrade the student's performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: deriving bayesian bounds for student knowledge distillation
PROPOSAL: Derive excess-risk bounds for the student's objective under probabilistic supervision, leveraging the Bayesian lens on knowledge distillation. Consider a teacher model that outputs noisy estimates of the true class posterior probabilities, and derive bounds in terms of the distance between these estimates and the true posteriors. Analyze how these bounds depend on the quality of the teacher's calibration and the level of noise in the teacher's predictions.
CONTROLS: Theoretical analysis of existing bounds derived in a Bayesian framework.
COST: 500 GPU-hours (available for theoretical derivations)
PREDICTION: We expect to obtain tighter bounds that relate the teacher's calibration and the level of noise in the teacher's predictions to the student's performance, providing a more principled understanding of knowledge distillation under probabilistic supervision.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: deriving bayesian bounds for student knowledge distillation
PROPOSAL: Derive excess-risk bounds for the student's objective under probabilistic supervision, leveraging the Bayesian lens on knowledge distillation. Consider a teacher model that outputs noisy estimates of the true class posterior probabilities, and derive bounds in terms of the distance between these estimates and the true posteriors. Analyze how these bounds depend on the quality of the teacher's calibration, the level of noise in the teacher's predictions, and the number of training samples.
CONTROLS: Theoretical analysis of existing bounds derived in a Bayesian framework.
COST: 500 GPU-hours (available for theoretical derivations)
PREDICTION: We expect to obtain tighter bounds that relate the teacher's calibration, the level of noise in the teacher's predictions, and the number of training samples to the student's performance, providing a more principled understanding of knowledge distillation under probabilistic supervision.

Additionally, the number of training samples (n) will provide interesting bounds. As n increases, the impact of the teacher's calibration and the level of noise decreases, bound will potentially degenerate into the risk for training. This is only a trivial example and real bounds can be complex.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: studying the effect of noise in teacher's estimates on student convergence
PROPOSAL: Investigate how the level and type of noise in the teacher's estimates of the true class posterior probabilities affect the student's convergence behavior. Use a partly correctly labeled dataset (e.g., corrupted versions of CIFAR-10 or ImageNet) and analyze the student's learning dynamics as a function of the noise level and its distribution. Compare the convergence behavior of the student when trained with different types of noise (e.g., Gaussian, uniform, batching noise).
CONTROLS: Baseline: training the student with perfectly labeled data; Ablations: varying the type and level of noise.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to observe an optimal level of noise above which the student's convergence degrades, and that the type of noise can significantly impact the student's learning behavior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: investigating the dynamics of sgd under probabilistic supervision
PROPOSAL: Study the optimization dynamics of SGD when used to train a student model under probabilistic supervision from a teacher model. Analyze how the teacher's estimation errors and the student's learning behavior are impacted by the choice of learning rate, batch size, and regularization. Explore the interplay between the student's convergence behavior and the teacher's calibration.
CONTROLS: Baseline: SGD with one-hot labels; Ablations: varying the learning rate, batch size, and regularization.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to gain insights into how SGD adapts under probabilistic supervision, and how the optimization dynamics depend on the learning parameters and the teacher's estimation accuracy.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: exploring the teacher's calibration in knowledge distillation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the relationship between the teacher's calibration and the student's performance under probabilistic supervision. Consider a teacher model that outputs noisy estimates of the true class posterior probabilities and analyze how the quality of these estimates affects the student's convergence, generalization, and accuracy. Use a dataset with ground-truth posterior probabilities (e.g., from a pre-trained teacher model) to evaluate the teacher's calibration and its impact on the student.
CONTROLS: Baseline: training the student with one-hot labels; Ablations: varying the teacher's temperature and estimation accuracy.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to identify a correlation between the teacher's calibration and the student's performance, and that improved teacher calibration leads to better student generalization and accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: analyzing teacher calibration for robust knowledge distillation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the relationship between teacher calibration and robustness in knowledge distillation. Design adversarial attacks on the student model that are induced by the teacher's noisy estimates of posterior probabilities, and analyze how teacher calibration affects the student's robustness to these attacks. Evaluate the robustness of the student model using metrics such as fooling rates and robust accuracy.
CONTROLS: Baseline: training the student with one-hot labels; Ablations: varying the teacher's temperature and estimation accuracy.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to demonstrate that teacher calibration has a significant impact on the student's robustness to adversarial attacks, and that improved teacher calibration leads to more robust student models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: comparing knowledge distillation with multiple teacher models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of using multiple teacher models with different calibrations on the student's performance and robustness. Train multiple teacher models with varying temperatures and estimation accuracies, and use the output of each teacher as soft labels for the student. Compare the performance of the student models trained with single and multiple teachers, and evaluate the trade-offs between performance, robustness, and complexity.
CONTROLS: Baseline: training the student with one-hot labels; Ablations: varying the number of teachers and their calibrations.
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to show that using multiple teacher models can improve the student's performance and robustness compared to single teacher models, but that the optimal combination of teachers depends on the problem and dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: investigating knowledge distillation for transfer learning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of knowledge distillation for transfer learning, where the teacher model is pre-trained on a different dataset and the student model is trained on a new, related dataset. Analyze the transfer of knowledge from the teacher to the student, and evaluate the impact of the teacher's calibration on the student's performance. Consider using domain adaptation techniques to align the teacher and student datasets.
CONTROLS: Baseline: training the student from scratch; Ablations: varying the pre-training dataset and transfer method.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to show that knowledge distillation can facilitate effective transfer learning, but that the choice of teacher model, calibration, and transfer method are critical to achieving good performance on the target dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: practically guiding teacher design for knowledge distillation
PROPOSAL: Develop practical guidelines for designing teacher models that produce better-provided supervision for students under knowledge distillation. Consider factors such as teacher model complexity, calibration quality, and dataset size, and analyze their impact on the student's performance and robustness. Develop a framework for selecting and tuning teacher models based on the specific requirements of the task and dataset.
CONTROLS: Baseline: training the teacher on a standard benchmark dataset; Ablations: varying the teacher model architecture, calibration, and dataset size.
COST: 2500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to provide a set of practical guidelines for designing teacher models that produce effective supervision for students, and to demonstrate the impact of these guidelines on the student's performance and robustness across various tasks and datasets.
